verdict.rationale: First-party docs cover each part of the story. Python editor scripting can automate asset tasks, place and lay out Actors in Levels, build import pipelines and drive custom UIs. Plugins can extend the Editor. C++ reflection metadata provides Editor functionality, and Remote Control lets external tools call Blueprint-callable functions. Python API reference and autocomplete stubs add depth. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of editor-automation workflows (the only community comment on scripting concerns runtime game modding, not editor tooling), and the Python API is marked Experimental.

support.subject: As a game developer, I can extend and automate the editor itself — custom tools, editor scripts, plugins that manipulate scenes and assets programmatically

citations.quote: Automate or randomize the placement, layout and settings of Actors in your Levels, Create your own Asset import and management pipelines
Plugins can add runtime gameplay functionality, modify built-in Engine features (or add new ones), create new file types, and extend the capabilities of the Editor
Automate time-consuming Asset management tasks in the Unreal Editor, like generating Levels of Detail (LODs) for Static Meshes.
Control the Unreal Editor from UIs that you create yourself in Python.
Using the Unreal Reflection System to encapsulate your classes with Metadata Property Specifier macros that provide Editor functionality
